en: to be dull; to be blunt

examples.ko: 칼이 너무 무뎌서 고기가 안 잘려요.
examples.en: The knife is so dull that it won't cut the meat.
The tip of the long-used pencil is blunt.
My hands lost feeling in the cold weather.
He tends to be slow at picking up on things.
Scissors with a dull blade are hard to use.

examples.ko: 사람이 너무 무디면 친구가 서운해할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you are too insensitive, your friends may feel hurt.

explain: '무디다'는 칼이나 연필처럼 날이나 끝이 날카롭지 않을 때도 쓰고, 사람의 감각이나 눈치가 둔할 때도 써요. 반대말은 '날카롭다'예요. '무뎌요', '무딘'으로 활용해요.

phrases.en: A dull knife is actually more dangerous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무디다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 활용형이에요. 날이 날카롭지 않은 칼을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, describing a knife that isn't sharp.

phrases.example: 추운 데 오래 있어서 손의 감각이 무뎌요.
phrases.en: I stayed in the cold a long time, so my hands feel numb.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 감각이나 느낌이 둔할 때 써요. 이때는 물건이 아니라 몸이나 마음에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person's senses or feelings are dull, about the body or mind rather than objects.

phrases.example: 이 칼은 무디지 않아서 잘 잘려요.
phrases.en: This knife isn't dull, so it cuts well.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 않다'로 부정하는 활용이에요. 날이 잘 선 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form with -지 않다, used for something with a good edge.

explain_en: Blades that don't cut well; also dull senses or wits. '무디다' works for a dull blade or tip, and also for a person who is slow to sense things or read the mood. The opposite is '날카롭다'. It conjugates as '무뎌요' and '무딘'.

t90.ax: The tip of the long-used pencil is blunt.

en: to be slippery; to be slimy

examples.en: My hands are slippery after lathering up with soap.
The floor is slippery, so be careful.

examples.ko: 미끌미끌한 생선은 소금으로 문지르면 잡기 편해요.
examples.en: If you rub a slimy fish with salt, it's easier to hold.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 계단이 미끌미끌해서 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The stairs were slippery from the rain, and I almost fell.

examples.ko: 기름이 묻어 미끌미끌했던 컵을 다시 씻었어요.
examples.en: I washed the cup again because it was slippery with oil.

examples.ko: 이 장갑은 안쪽이 미끌미끌하지 않아서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like these gloves because the inside isn't slippery.

explain: 손에 쥐기 어렵거나 발이 미끄러질 만큼 표면이 매끄러울 때 써요. 비누, 기름, 물기처럼 원인이 되는 것이 같이 나오는 경우가 많아요. 말할 때 '미끌미끌'은 가볍고 귀여운 느낌이라 일상 대화에서도 편하게 써요.

phrases.en: The road is slippery because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻의 더 일반적인 말이고 바닥에 특히 잘 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general word with the same meaning, especially for floors.

phrases.example: 욕실의 미끌미끌한 바닥 때문에 넘어질 뻔했어요.
phrases.en: I almost fell because of the slippery bathroom floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: My hands are slippery, so it's hard to hold the cup.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아서/어서'로 이유를 이어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -아서/어서 to connect a reason.

explain_en: Use it when a surface is so smooth that it's hard to grip or your foot might slide. The cause, such as soap, oil or water, often appears in the same sentence. '미끌미끌' sounds light and a bit cute, so it fits easily into everyday conversation.

t90.ax: The floor is slippery, so be careful.

examples.ko: 이 용기는 밀폐가 잘 돼서 냄새가 안 새요.
examples.en: This container seals well, so the smell doesn't leak out.
Please store kimchi in an airtight container.

examples.ko: 창문 밀폐를 잘하면 겨울에 난방비가 줄어요.
examples.en: If you seal the windows well, your heating bill goes down in winter.

examples.ko: 완전한 밀폐는 어려워서 약간의 공기는 들어가요.
examples.en: A complete seal is difficult, so a little air gets in.

examples.ko: 밀폐 포장 덕분에 과자가 눅눅해지지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the airtight packaging, the snacks didn't go soggy.
I bought a new lid with good sealing power.

explain: 틈 없이 막아서 공기나 물이 통하지 않는 느낌이라 단순한 '닫음'과 달라요. 주방용품에서는 '밀폐 용기'가 가장 흔한 말이에요. 반대는 '개방'이고, 공기를 통하게 하는 일은 '환기'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 남은 반찬은 밀폐 용기에 담아 두세요.
phrases.en: Please keep the leftover side dishes in an airtight container.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주방에서 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in the kitchen.

phrases.en: You need to be careful about gas in an enclosed space.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공기가 잘 통하지 않는 좁은 장소를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a closed-off place where air doesn't circulate.

phrases.en: Seal the bag tightly and put it in the freezer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '밀폐'를 동사로 써서 틈 없이 막는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form, meaning to close something up tightly.

explain_en: Airtight closing so liquid or air cannot leak (밀폐 용기) It carries the feel of closing with no gaps so air or water can't pass, which is different from simply closing something. '밀폐 용기' (airtight container) is the most common phrase for kitchenware. The opposite is '개방', and letting air in is called '환기'.

t90.ax: I bought a new lid with good sealing power.

examples.en: I stayed in my room the whole weekend.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 청소했더니 방구석에 먼지가 많이 쌓여 있었어요.
examples.en: I cleaned for the first time in a while, and dust had piled up in the corner of the room.
One sock turned up in the corner of the room.
The child got scolded and went into a corner of the room to cry.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 방구석만 지키고 있기 답답해요.
examples.en: It's stifling to stay cooped up in my room all day.
The remote must be somewhere in a corner of the room.

explain: 방 안의 구석이라는 뜻도 있지만, 집이나 방에만 틀어박혀 있는 모습을 투덜거리듯 말할 때도 많이 써요. 말투가 편해서 글보다 대화에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I want to rest at home in my room on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집이나 방에서 편하게 쉬는 모습을 가볍게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say you are relaxing in your room or at home.

phrases.en: I played games in my room all day long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밖에 나가지 않고 방에만 있는 모습을 투덜거리듯 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says in a grumbling tone that someone stays in the room and never goes out.
phrases.en_equiv: to just play games shut in one's room

phrases.example: 청소를 안 했더니 방구석에 먼지가 쌓였어요.
phrases.en: I didn't clean, so dust piled up in the corner of the room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방 안의 구석이라는 원래 뜻으로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the literal meaning, a corner inside a room.
phrases.en_equiv: dust piles up in the corner of a room

explain_en: Corner of a room; casual, often suggests staying home idly. It can mean a corner inside a room, but it is also used in a grumbling tone for staying shut up at home or in your room. The tone is casual, so it fits conversation better than formal writing.

examples.en: I boiled instant noodles on a burner at the campsite.
I need to put new gas in the burner.

examples.ko: 바람이 불어서 버너 불이 자꾸 꺼져요.
examples.en: The wind keeps blowing out the burner flame.
I took a small burner when I went hiking.

examples.ko: 버너를 쓸 때는 불 조심을 해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful with fire when using a burner.

examples.ko: 친구가 새 버너를 사서 같이 써 봤어요.
examples.en: My friend bought a new burner and we tried it together.

explain: '버너'는 밖에서 요리할 때 쓰는 휴대용 불판이에요. 집 부엌에서 쓰는 건 '가스레인지'나 '인덕션'이라고 해요. 캠핑 이야기에서 '버너'와 '코펠'을 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: We grilled meat on a gas burner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가스로 불을 켜는 버너를 말하고, 캠핑에서 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A burner lit with gas, the most common kind for camping.

phrases.en: I turned on the burner and boiled water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불을 붙일 때 '켜다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '켜다' when turning on the flame.

phrases.en: I put the portable burner in my backpack.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들고 다닐 수 있다는 점을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear that it can be carried around.

explain_en: '버너' is a portable stove for cooking outdoors. The ones in a home kitchen are a '가스레인지' or '인덕션'. In camping talk it often comes together with '코펠', the cooking pot set.

examples.en: Try turning the screw with a Phillips screwdriver.
Please take a Phillips screwdriver out of the drawer.
I didn't have a Phillips screwdriver, so I opened it with a coin.
A Phillips screwdriver fits this screw.
My father always keeps the Phillips screwdriver in the toolbox.
We need to buy one Phillips and one flat-head screwdriver.

explain: 나사 머리가 '+' 모양이면 십자드라이버, '-' 모양이면 '일자드라이버'를 써요. 일상에서는 그냥 '드라이버'라고 줄여 말하기도 해요. 머리카락 말리는 '드라이어'와 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: I tighten the screw with a screwdriver.
phrases.nuance_ko: 십자드라이버를 일상에서 짧게 줄여 말한 거예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The everyday shortened form of the term.

phrases.en: I loosened the screw with a Phillips screwdriver.
phrases.nuance_ko: '+' 모양 나사를 풀 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for loosening '+' shaped screws.
phrases.en_equiv: to loosen with a Phillips screwdriver

phrases.en: You need a Phillips screwdriver to assemble this chair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조립이나 수리 설명서에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen in assembly or repair instructions.

explain_en: Use a 십자드라이버 for screws with a '+' head and a '일자드라이버' for a '-' head. In daily speech people often just say '드라이버'. Don't confuse it with '드라이어' (hair dryer).

en: to let (a fire) go out; to put out

examples.en: I put out the candle by mistake.
Be careful not to let the campfire go out.
The wind is strong, so I keep letting the match go out.

examples.ko: 난로 불씨를 꺼뜨리면 다시 피우기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you let the stove embers die, it's hard to light them again.

examples.ko: 아기가 후 불어서 생일 초를 다 꺼뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The baby blew and put out all the birthday candles.
I stalled the engine and the car stopped suddenly.

explain: '끄다'는 일부러 끌 때 쓰고, '꺼뜨리다'는 실수나 부주의로 불이 꺼지게 했을 때 많이 써요. '꺼트리다'로도 써요. 불, 촛불, 불씨뿐 아니라 운전할 때 '시동을 꺼뜨리다'처럼도 말해요.

phrases.en: The wind blew and put out the candle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꺼뜨리다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 다른 표기예요. 둘 다 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: An alternative spelling with the same meaning as '꺼뜨리다'. Both are correct.

phrases.example: 캠핑장에서 불씨를 꺼뜨리지 않으려고 장작을 더 넣었어요.
phrases.en: At the campsite I added more firewood so the embers wouldn't die out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불씨나 모닥불을 잘 지키지 못해서 꺼지게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you fail to keep embers or a campfire alive and it goes out.

phrases.en: I stalled the car on a hill and panicked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운전할 때 실수로 차의 시동이 꺼지게 했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means accidentally stalling the engine while driving.

explain_en: '끄다' is for turning something off on purpose, while '꺼뜨리다' often suggests you let a fire go out by mistake or carelessness. You can also say '꺼트리다'. It is used for fires, candles and embers, and also in driving, as in '시동을 꺼뜨리다' (to stall the engine).

examples.ko: 엄마가 아무리 깨워도 동생은 꿈쩍하지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how much Mom wakes him, my brother doesn't stir.

examples.ko: 너무 추워서 이불 밖으로 꿈쩍하기도 싫어요.
examples.en: It's so cold that I don't even want to budge out from under the blanket.
This tree didn't budge even in the typhoon.

examples.ko: 책상이 너무 무거워서 둘이 밀어도 꿈쩍할 기미가 없어요.
examples.en: The desk is so heavy that it shows no sign of moving even when two people push.

examples.ko: 제가 부탁해도 그 사람은 꿈쩍하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even when I asked, that person wouldn't budge.
Today I don't want to move from the sofa.

explain: '꿈쩍도 하지 않다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 쓰는 경우가 대부분이에요. 물건이 안 움직일 때뿐 아니라 사람의 마음이나 태도가 안 바뀔 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 아무리 설득해도 그는 꿈쩍도 하지 않아요.
phrases.en: No matter how much I try to persuade him, he doesn't budge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이나 태도가 조금도 바뀌지 않는다는 뜻으로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say someone's mind or attitude doesn't change at all.

phrases.en: I was so shocked that I couldn't move for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: '않다'는 움직이지 않는 것이고, '못하다'는 움직이고 싶어도 못 움직이는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '않다' means not moving; '못하다' means being unable to move even if you want to.

phrases.example: 발이 꽁꽁 얼어서 꿈쩍할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: My feet are frozen stiff, so I can't move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상황이나 몸 상태 때문에 움직일 수 없을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can't move because of the situation or your physical condition.

explain_en: It is mostly used in negative forms like '꿈쩍도 하지 않다'. You can say it about objects that won't move, and also about a person's mind or attitude that won't change.

examples.en: I do the ironing on Sunday evening.
I'm clumsy at ironing, so the shirt got wrinkled.

examples.ko: 다리미질 후에는 꼭 전원을 꺼야 해요.
examples.en: After ironing you must turn off the power.
My mother is very skilled at ironing.
I listened to a drama while ironing.
Ironing takes longer than you'd think.

explain: 다리미로 옷을 펴는 일이에요. 보통 '다리미질을 하다'라고 말하고, '다림질'이라고도 해요. 말할 때는 '옷을 다리다'라고 하는 경우도 많아요.

phrases.en: If I iron, my clothes look neat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '다리미질'과 같은 뜻이고 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '다리미질' and the more common form.

phrases.en: I do the ironing on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 뒤에 '을 하다'를 붙여 일하는 동작을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '을 하다' to the noun expresses the act of doing the task.

phrases.en: When the ironing is done, I'll clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝났다는 뜻을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say the task is finished.

explain_en: It is the work of smoothing clothes with an iron. You usually say '다리미질을 하다', and '다림질' is also used. In speech, people also often say '옷을 다리다'.

t90.ax: I do the ironing on Sunday evening.

en: to exaggerate; to brag; to boast

examples.ko: 그는 자기 자랑을 온 동네에 떠벌리고 다녀요.
examples.en: He goes around bragging about himself all over the neighborhood.
Please don't blab the secret to your friends.

examples.ko: 별것 아닌 일을 크게 떠벌려서 민망했어요.
examples.en: He blew a trivial matter out of proportion, and it was embarrassing.
He bragged all day long about winning an award.
You shouldn't spread family matters to just anybody.

examples.ko: 자기 얘기를 떠벌리는 사람은 좀 부담스러워요.
examples.en: People who talk loudly about themselves are a bit much for me.

explain: 자랑이나 비밀, 별것 아닌 일을 크게 부풀리거나 여기저기 말하고 다닐 때 써요. 그냥 '말하다'나 '자랑하다'보다 시끄럽게 널리 퍼뜨린다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 칭찬하는 상황에는 잘 안 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그 얘기를 여기저기 떠벌리고 다니지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't go around blabbing that story everywhere.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여기저기 다니며 말을 퍼뜨리는 모습을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes going around spreading a story everywhere.

phrases.en: He brags every time we meet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자랑을 시끄럽게 늘어놓는다는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a negative feel of loudly going on about one's boasts.

phrases.example: 친구가 내 비밀을 온 동네에 떠벌렸어요.
phrases.en: My friend blabbed my secret all over the neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨겨야 할 이야기를 여기저기 말해 버릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone spreads a story that should have been kept secret.

explain_en: Spoken, negative — loudly boasting or spreading talk about oneself. Use it when someone inflates a boast, a secret or a trivial matter, or goes around telling it to everyone. Compared with plain '말하다' or '자랑하다', it adds a negative feeling of noisily spreading something widely. It doesn't fit praising situations.

t90.ax: Please don't blab the secret to your friends.

en: to be satisfied; to be fulfilled

examples.ko: 조건이 모두 만족되면 신청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can apply once all conditions are met.

examples.ko: 수요가 만족되자 줄을 서는 사람이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Once the demand was met, fewer people stood in line.
The demand was not satisfied, so I complained.

examples.ko: 이 식이 만족되는 숫자를 찾아 보세요.
examples.en: Find the number that satisfies this equation.
All standards were satisfied.

examples.ko: 필요가 만족된 뒤에는 더 사지 않아요.
examples.en: After the need is met, I do not buy more.

explain: 기분이 좋다는 '만족하다'와 달리, 조건이나 요구가 채워졌다는 쪽에 자주 써요. 수학과 서류에서도 나와요. 사람이 느끼는 만족은 '만족하다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 조건이 만족되지 않아서 신청할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: This condition is not met, so I can't apply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건이 채워지지 않았다는 뜻으로 서류에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a condition has not been fulfilled; common in paperwork.

phrases.en: The customer's demands need to be met.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요구나 필요가 채워진다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means a demand or need is fulfilled.

phrases.en: When people's demand is satisfied, prices go down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고 싶어 하는 양이 충분히 채워졌다는 뜻으로 경제 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the amount people want is fully supplied; used in talk about the economy.

explain_en: Conditions or wishes get fulfilled — passive, things not people. Unlike '만족하다', which is about feeling pleased, '만족되다' is often about conditions or demands being fulfilled. It also appears in math and paperwork. A person's feeling of satisfaction is '만족하다'.

dis.h: a condition or wish gets fulfilled
gh: needs or requirements get fully met; formal

p.n: 충족되다 is more common and formal for requirements being met.

examples.en: Three people survived the accident.
It is hard for animals to survive without water.
I learned how to survive on a deserted island.

examples.ko: 그들은 추위 속에서 일주일 동안 생존할 수 있었어요.
examples.en: They were able to survive for a week in the cold.
For a small shop to survive, it needs customers.
What if dinosaurs still survived?

explain: '살아남다'는 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰고, '생존하다'는 뉴스와 글에서 자주 나와요. 사고, 재난, 자연처럼 어려운 상황 속에서 목숨이 이어질 때 써요. 가게나 회사가 '버티다'는 의미로도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: Three people survived the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common word in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The survivors of the accident are in the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 살아남은 사람을 부르는 말로 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for a person who survived, common in news.

phrases.en: It is hard to survive in the desert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경이 힘들어서 살아가기 어렵다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the environment makes survival hard.

explain_en: Formal; remain alive through danger or harsh conditions; survivors. 살아남다 is more common in everyday talk, while 생존하다 appears in news and writing. It is used when life continues through difficult situations such as accidents, disasters or nature. It can also be used figuratively for a shop or company holding on.

examples.en: Fruit needs washing before you eat it.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 자동 세척 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: This machine has an automatic cleaning function.
Cleaning tools is really important in a hospital.
Please wipe off the water after washing.

examples.ko: 주방 세제는 그릇 세척에만 써야 해요.
examples.en: Kitchen soap should only be used for washing dishes.
I put the washed vegetables in a basket.

explain: '세척'은 물이나 세제로 더러운 것을 씻어 내는 일이에요. 손이나 얼굴은 '씻다', 옷은 '빨다'라고 하고, '세척'은 과일·도구·기계·상처처럼 기술적인 대상에 많이 써요. 설명서에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I cleaned the cup well with this cleaning agent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더러운 것을 씻는 데 쓰는 물질을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a substance used for cleaning dirty things.

phrases.example: 이 병은 입구가 넓어서 세척이 쉬워요.
phrases.en: This bottle has a wide opening, so it's easy to clean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도구나 기계가 씻기 편한지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say whether a tool or machine is easy to wash.

phrases.en: After dinner, I run the dishwasher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그릇을 자동으로 씻는 기계 이름이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name of the machine that washes dishes automatically.

explain_en: Wash dirt off objects or produce (과일 세척) 세척 is washing away dirt with water or cleaner. For hands and face you say 씻다 and for clothes 빨다, while 세척 is used for fruit, tools, machines, and wounds. It appears often in manuals.

t90.ax: Fruit needs washing before you eat it.
